explanations: There is no defect. Rendering happens outside the lock, so concurrent misses for the same key may render twice, but try_emplace keeps the first inserted value and every caller receives a valid shared_ptr, so the duplication is only wasted work. The cache returns shared_ptr<const std::string>, so clear() on eviction cannot invalidate a playlist a caller is still using. The string is pre-sized with reserve and numbers are formatted with to_chars, avoiding repeated reallocation and stream overhead. The relaxed atomics are fine because the histogram buckets are independent counters read only for reporting.

The shared lock is released at the end of the inner block before rendering, and rendering holds no lock, so both threads can render. try_emplace does not overwrite an existing key; the later thread receives the first thread's entry. No lock is held while upgrading, so there is no deadlock, and shared_ptr ownership keeps any returned string alive.

clear() only drops the cache's reference. Each caller holds its own shared_ptr<const std::string>, so the string is destroyed after the last reference goes away. Returning a raw reference or string_view from the cache would have the dangling problem described; here it does not occur. The data is const, so concurrent readers are safe.

record() halves 300 repeatedly while us > 1: 300 -> 150 -> 75 -> 37 -> 18 -> 9 -> 4 -> 2 -> 1, which is 8 shifts, so idx = 8, meaning [256, 512) microseconds. There are only 16 buckets, so index 300 does not exist, and 9 or 7 would correspond to different ranges.
